summary: Alfred Horsford Bingley worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He was educated at Kensington School and studied at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst around 1884 to 1885.

Alfred Körte studied at the University of Bonn (1886-1890) and worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He held posts at Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig (~1917-1934).

Alfred Louis Noël de Sadous worked in Indology, studying under Eugène Burnouf and earning his dr.-ès-lettres from the University of Paris by 1847. He taught as a professor of troisième at the Lycée Hoche.

Alfred Ludwig worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Vienna and Berlin under Weber, Boller, Bonitz, Boeckh, Haupt, and Müller. He habilitated at Vienna (1858) before serving as professor at Charles University (1860-1901).

Alfred Master worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Epsom College and Oxford (D.Phil.). He served as a lecturer and governing body member at SOAS (1937-1960) and assistant keeper at the India Office Records (1951-1957).

Alfred North Whitehead was a philosopher who studied at Sherborne School, Trinity College, Cambridge, and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at Cambridge (1884-1910), Imperial College London (1914-1924), and Harvard University (1924-1937).

Alfred Nottrott worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1860) and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (~1885-1887), serving as a missionary for the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church from 1867.

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at King Edward's School, Trinity College, and the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers. He held posts at the University of Sydney, University of Chicago, University of Oxford, and FESP in São Paulo.

Alfred Roussel was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Collège de Saint-Malo, Major Seminary of Rennes, and under Abel Bergaigne and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault. He was professor of Sanskrit at the University of Fribourg (1903-1920).

Alfred Schmitt worked in linguistics, studying at Gnadenfeld Theological Seminary and the University of Rostock under Gustav Herbig and Hermann Güntert. He held posts at Rostock (1928-1935), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1935-1941), and Münster (1941-1956).

Alfred Shenington Geden worked in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies after studying at Oxford and Aberdeen. He was principal at Royapettah College (1886-1889) and taught at Richmond College (~1891-1920) and Wesleyan College (1891-1915).

Alfred William Stratton worked in Indology and linguistics after studying at Toronto and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He taught at Chicago (1895-1899) and served as principal of Oriental College and at the University of the Punjab (~1899-1902).

Alfred von Gutschmid studied at Leipzig and Bonn under Christian Lassen, working in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held professorships at Kiel, Königsberg, Jena, and Tübingen (1877).

Alfredo Trombetti worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Bologna (~1886-1891) and later served there as professor of Semitic Philology (from 1904) and professor of Glottology (from 1912).
Ali Beth was an Indologist who completed their doctorate at Utrecht University in 1943 under the supervision of Jan Gonda.

Ali S. Asani works in religious studies and Indology. After studying at Harvard College and Harvard University, he became Murray A. Albertson Professor of Middle Eastern Studies and Professor of Indo-Muslim and Islamic Religion and Cultures at Harvard (~1983).

Alice Harris is a linguist who studied at Harvard University and the University of Massachusetts Amherst. She held academic posts at Vanderbilt University (~1979-2009) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2009).
Alice Margaret Stevenson worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Somerville College, Trinity College Dublin, and Oxford, where she studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Alice Y. Tseng works in Japanology and history and archaeology. She was a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang and is attested as a professor at Boston University in 2013.

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, also studying with other teachers, and became an associate professor at York University in 2009.
